# Build graph object

----

Basic workflow of **ggNetView**：

1. Build a **graph object**
2. Understand and manipulate the **graph object**
3. Visualize the network using **layout algorithms**
4. Retrieve **topology** of network

----


> Load R Package


```{r warning=F, message=F}
library(tidyverse)   # data manipulation / piping utilities
library(ggNetView)   # graph builders + info-extraction helpers
library(igraph)      # igraph object
```

----

## Build graph from matrix

>  Example data

```{r}
# ---- Built-in example datasets shipped with ggNetView ----

# Raw ASV/OTU abundance table (rows = ASVs/OTUs, cols = samples; integer counts).
data("otu_tab")
dim(otu_tab)
otu_tab[1:5, 1:5]

# Same table after rarefaction (sequencing depth normalised across samples).
data("otu_rare")
dim(otu_rare)
otu_rare[1:5, 1:5]

# Rarefied table converted to relative abundance — most common input for correlation networks.
data("otu_rare_relative")
dim(otu_rare_relative)
otu_rare_relative[1:5, 1:5]

# Taxonomic annotation for the ASVs/OTUs above.
# First column must be the ASV/OTU ID (matches rownames of the abundance tables).
data("tax_tab")
dim(tax_tab)
tax_tab[1:5, 1:5]
```

> Build graph object

```{r message=F}
# ---- Build a co-occurrence network directly from an abundance matrix ----
# Internal pipeline: transform -> correlation -> p-value adjustment ->
# edge filtering -> community detection -> attach taxonomy.
graph_obj <- build_graph_from_mat(
  mat              = otu_rare_relative,  # variables x samples numeric matrix
  transfrom.method = "none",             # input is already relative abundance, no extra transform
  r.threshold      = 0.7,                # |r| cutoff (subjective; consider ggNetView_RMT)
  p.threshold      = 0.05,               # adjusted p-value cutoff
  method           = "WGCNA",            # correlation backend: WGCNA::corAndPvalue
  cor.method       = "pearson",          # Pearson correlation
  proc             = "bonferroni",       # multiple-testing correction
  module.method    = "Fast_greedy",      # community detection algorithm
  node_annotation  = tax_tab,            # taxonomy joined onto each node by name
  top_modules      = 15,                 # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed             = 1115                # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

# Inspect node/edge counts and the columns now attached to nodes:
# modularity, modularity2, modularity3, Modularity, Degree, Strength + taxonomy.
graph_obj
```

## Build graph from data frame

>  Example data

```{r}
# Edge-list style example data (protein-protein interactions).
data("ppi_example")

# `df`: edge list — typically 3 columns: node1 | node2 | weight (weight optional).
df = ppi_example$ppi
head(df)

# `node_annotation`: per-node metadata; first column = node ID.
node_annotation = ppi_example$annotation
head(node_annotation)
```

> Build graph object

```{r message=F}
# ---- Build a tbl_graph directly from an edge-list data.frame ----
# No correlation step — edges are taken as-is from `df`.
# Community detection still runs on the resulting graph.
graph_obj_from_df <- build_graph_from_df(
  df              = df,                # edge list (node1 | node2 | weight)
  node_annotation = node_annotation,   # per-node metadata, joined by node name
  directed        = F,                 # undirected network
  module.method   = "Fast_greedy",     # community detection algorithm
  top_modules     = 15,                # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed            = 1115               # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_from_df
```


```{r message=F}
# ---- Same builder, but WITHOUT a node-annotation table ----
# Useful when only an edge list is available and no extra metadata to attach.
graph_obj_from_df2 <- build_graph_from_df(
  df              = df,                # edge list
  node_annotation = NULL,              # skip the annotation join entirely
  directed        = F,                 # undirected network
  module.method   = "Fast_greedy",     # community detection algorithm
  top_modules     = 15,                # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed            = 1115               # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_from_df2
```

## Build graph from data frame with module

>  Example data

```{r}
# Same shape as ppi_example, but `annotation` already contains a `Modularity`
# column (module assignments computed elsewhere — we will NOT recompute them).
data("ppi_module")

df = ppi_module$ppi
head(df)

node_annotation = ppi_module$annotation
head(node_annotation)   # NOTE: must contain a `Modularity` column
```

> Build graph object

```{r message=F}
# ---- `_module` variant: keep pre-computed module assignments ----
# Use this when you already have modules (e.g. from a previous WGCNA run,
# expert curation, biological prior). Internal community detection is skipped.
graph_obj_from_module <- build_graph_from_module(
  df              = df,                # edge list
  node_annotation = node_annotation,   # MUST contain a `Modularity` column
  directed        = F,                 # undirected network
  top_modules     = 15,                # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed            = 1115               # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_from_module
```

## Build graph from adjacency matrix

>  Example data

```{r}
# Square adjacency matrix (already-filtered weights for every node pair).
# Useful when the network was built externally (NetCoMi, FlashWeave, ...).
data("adjacency_matrix_example")
dim(adjacency_matrix_example)
adjacency_matrix_example[1:5, 1:5]

# Reuse the same taxonomy table as node annotation.
data("tax_tab")
dim(tax_tab)
tax_tab[1:5, 1:5]
```


> Build graph object

```{r message=F}
# ---- Build a tbl_graph from a pre-computed adjacency matrix ----
# Community detection runs internally because we have weights but no modules yet.
graph_obj_adj <- build_graph_from_adj_mat(
  adjacency_matrix = adjacency_matrix_example, # square weighted adjacency matrix
  module.method    = "Fast_greedy",            # community detection algorithm
  node_annotation  = tax_tab,                  # per-node metadata, joined by node name
  top_modules      = 15,                       # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed             = 1115                      # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_adj
```

## Build graph from adjacency matrix with module information

```{r}
# Add a pre-existing module assignment to the annotation table.
# (Demo only) treat the `Kingdom` column as the module label;
# in real use, supply your actual module assignments.
tax_tab_module <- tax_tab %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Modularity = Kingdom)
```


```{r}
# ---- `_module` variant for adjacency input ----
# REQUIRES `node_annotation` to contain a `Modularity` column.
# Internal community detection is skipped; supplied modules are used directly.
graph_obj_adj_module <- build_graph_from_adj_mat_module(
  adjacency_matrix = adjacency_matrix_example, # square weighted adjacency matrix
  node_annotation  = tax_tab_module,           # MUST contain a `Modularity` column
  top_modules      = 15,                       # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed             = 1115                      # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_adj_module
```

## Build graph from double matrix

>  Example data

```{r}
# Two abundance matrices on the SAME samples but DIFFERENT feature sets,
# typically used for cross-kingdom networks (e.g. bacteria <-> fungi).

# Bacterial ASV table.
data("BASV_tab")
dim(BASV_tab)
BASV_tab[1:5, 1:5]

# Fungal ASV table.
data("FASV_tab")
dim(FASV_tab)
FASV_tab[1:5, 1:5]

# Combined node-annotation table covering BOTH feature sets above.
data("double_mat_node_df")
dim(double_mat_node_df)
head(double_mat_node_df)
```


> Build graph object

```{r}
# ---- Cross-domain (bipartite-style) network ----
# Correlations are computed BETWEEN features in mat1 and features in mat2
# (no within-mat1 / within-mat2 edges), then thresholded, modularised,
# and joined with the node-annotation table.
graph_obj_double_mat <- build_graph_from_double_mat(
  mat1            = BASV_tab,            # set A (e.g. bacteria), variables x samples
  mat2            = FASV_tab,            # set B (e.g. fungi),    variables x samples
  module.method   = "Fast_greedy",       # community detection algorithm
  node_annotation = double_mat_node_df,  # node metadata covering BOTH mat1 and mat2
  top_modules     = 15,                  # keep top-15 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed            = 1115                 # fix RNG for reproducibility
)
graph_obj_double_mat
```


## Build graph from igraph object

```{r}
# Load the PPI example dataset (edge list + node annotation).
data("ppi_example")

# Build a native igraph object directly from the edge list.
# This is the format users coming from an igraph workflow typically already have.
igraph_object <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  d        = ppi_example$ppi,          # edge list
  vertices = ppi_example$annotation,   # vertex metadata
  directed = FALSE                     # undirected network
)

igraph_object

# ---- Convert an existing igraph object into a ggNetView-compatible tbl_graph ----
# Adds Modularity / Degree / Strength columns and harmonises the schema so it
# plugs straight into ggNetView().
graph_obj_from_igraph <- build_graph_from_igraph(
  igraph        = igraph_object,   # an existing igraph object
  module.method = "Fast_greedy",   # community detection algorithm
  seed          = 1115             # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

graph_obj_from_igraph
```


## Build graph from WGCNA

```
# ---- Importing an existing WGCNA pipeline output ----
# (Not evaluated here — requires external files saved by WGCNA::blockwiseModules.)

# 1. Load the topological overlap matrix (TOM) saved by WGCNA.
load(file = "WGCNA.tom-block.1.RData")
TOM_mat <- as.matrix(TOM)

# 2. Load the abundance matrix used to build that TOM
#    (kept for downstream re-thresholding / sanity checks).
plot.mat = readRDS(file = "plot.mat.Rds")

# 3. Sparsify the TOM: keep only the top_k strongest TOM connections per node.
trans_TOM <- trans_TOM_in_WGCNA(
  TOM_mat,     # square TOM matrix from WGCNA
  plot.mat,    # original abundance matrix the TOM came from
  top_k = 1    # keep top_k strongest neighbours per node
)

# 4. Load the WGCNA net object (contains module colour assignments).
net <- readRDS(file = "net.Rds")

# 5. Build the module table — one row per feature; columns: ID + Module.
module <- data.frame(
  ID     = names(net$colors),          # feature IDs
  Module = as.character(net$colors)    # WGCNA module colour as module label
)

# 6. Optional ordering of node IDs (used as node_annotation here).
id <- data.frame(
  ID = names(sort(net$colors))         # node IDs in module order
)

# 7. Assemble the tbl_graph.
#    Uses the sparsified TOM as edge weights and the WGCNA module colours as
#    the Modularity assignment (no community detection is recomputed).
obj <- build_graph_from_wgcna(
  wgcna_tom       = trans_TOM,  # sparsified TOM (from trans_TOM_in_WGCNA)
  module          = module,     # data.frame with ID + Module columns
  node_annotation = id          # optional per-node metadata
)
obj
```

## Build graph from multi-graph 

```{r}
# ---- Consensus-network workflow ----
# (1) Build several per-method networks from the SAME matrix.
# (2) Convert each tbl_graph back to an adjacency matrix.
# (3) Fuse the per-method adjacencies into ONE consensus tbl_graph.

# Restrict to the 40 most abundant OTUs to keep this chunk responsive.
data(otu_rare_relative)
mat <- as.matrix(otu_rare_relative)
mat <- mat[order(rowSums(mat), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(40)], ]

# ---- (1) Three per-method networks on the same data ----

# Spearman correlation through psych::corr.test — baseline method.
g_cor   <- build_graph_from_mat(
  mat,                              # input matrix (variables x samples)
  method        = "cor",            # correlation backend: psych::corr.test
  cor.method    = "spearman",       # Spearman correlation
  proc          = "BH",             # multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg)
  r.threshold   = 0.4,              # |r| cutoff
  p.threshold   = 0.05,             # adjusted p-value cutoff
  module.method = "Fast_greedy",    # community detection algorithm
  seed          = 1                 # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

# WGCNA-style correlation (WGCNA::corAndPvalue + the package's thresholding).
g_wgcna <- build_graph_from_mat(
  mat,                              # input matrix (variables x samples)
  method        = "WGCNA",          # correlation backend: WGCNA::corAndPvalue
  cor.method    = "spearman",       # Spearman correlation
  proc          = "BH",             # multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg)
  r.threshold   = 0.4,              # |r| cutoff
  p.threshold   = 0.05,             # adjusted p-value cutoff
  module.method = "Fast_greedy",    # community detection algorithm
  seed          = 1                 # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

# Hmisc::rcorr — another correlation engine; slightly different NA/tie behaviour.
g_hmisc <- build_graph_from_mat(
  mat,                              # input matrix (variables x samples)
  method        = "Hmisc",          # correlation backend: Hmisc::rcorr
  cor.method    = "spearman",       # Spearman correlation
  r.threshold   = 0.4,              # |r| cutoff
  p.threshold   = 0.05,             # raw p-value cutoff (no `proc` here)
  module.method = "Fast_greedy",    # community detection algorithm
  seed          = 1                 # fix RNG for reproducibility
)

# ---- (2) tbl_graph -> adjacency matrix ----
# `get_graph_adjacency()` recovers the weighted adjacency matrix from a tbl_graph,
# which is the format expected by build_graph_from_consensus().
adj_cor   <- get_graph_adjacency(g_cor)
adj_wgcna <- get_graph_adjacency(g_wgcna)
adj_hmisc <- get_graph_adjacency(g_hmisc)

# Bundle per-method matrices into a NAMED list.
# Names ("cor", "wgcna", "hmisc") are kept as method labels downstream.
adj_list <- list(cor = adj_cor, wgcna = adj_wgcna, hmisc = adj_hmisc)

# ---- (3) Consensus fusion ----
# Borda rank fusion: ranks every pair by |w| in each method, averages the ranks,
# then min-max rescales to [-1, 1]. Robust to per-method weight-scale differences.
g_borda <- build_graph_from_consensus(
  adj_list              = adj_list,        # named list of per-method adjacency matrices
  method                = "rank_fusion",   # fusion strategy
  rank_fusion_algorithm = "borda",         # specific rank-fusion variant
  threshold             = 0.5,             # final |w| cutoff applied to the fused matrix
  top_modules           = 5,               # keep top-5 modules; rest -> "Others"
  seed                  = 1                # fix RNG for reproducibility
)
g_borda
```
